---
name: database-migration
description: Change the PostgreSQL schema or seed data of AI Workspace safely with Flyway, keeping the JPA entities, domain model and tests in sync. Use this when a feature needs a new table, column, index or constraint, or a data fix.
---

# Database migration

Flyway owns the schema. Hibernate only validates it (`spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto: validate`), so the application
refuses to start when entities and tables disagree.

## Rules

- Migrations live in `backend/src/main/resources/db/migration` and are named `V<next number>__<snake_case_description>.sql`
  (two underscores), for example `V3__add_message_attachments.sql`. Check the highest existing number first.
- **Never edit or delete a migration that has been applied anywhere** (checksums are validated at startup). Fix
  mistakes with a new migration. Flyway Community has no undo, so rollbacks are forward migrations too.
- Follow the existing style: upper-case SQL keywords, `UUID` primary keys (generated by the application),
  `TIMESTAMPTZ` for instants, `VARCHAR(n)` plus a `CHECK` constraint for enums stored as strings, and
  `ON DELETE CASCADE` for owned children.
- Naming: tables plural snake_case; indexes `ix_<table>_<columns>`, unique indexes `ux_<table>_<columns>`, checks
  `chk_<table>_<column>`.
- Seed data uses fixed UUIDs (see `V2__seed_system_prompts.sql`) so that later migrations can reference or update
  those rows. Use `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` when the rows might already exist (for example, created by an
  administrator).
- Keep migrations backwards-compatible with the running version where possible: add nullable columns or columns with
  defaults first, backfill, then tighten constraints in a later migration.
- Long-running index builds on large tables: `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` cannot run inside a transaction. Put it in its
  own migration with a script config file `V<n>__<name>.sql.conf` containing `executeInTransaction=false`.

## Steps

1. Write `V<n>__<description>.sql`.
2. Update the JPA entity in `infrastructure/persistence/entity` (`@Column` names, lengths, nullability and
   `@Enumerated(EnumType.STRING)` must match the SQL) and, if needed, the Spring Data repository in
   `infrastructure/persistence/jpa`.
3. Update the domain model (`domain/<aggregate>`) and the mapping in `infrastructure/persistence/adapter`. Domain
   objects never reference JPA types.
4. Extend the repository port in `domain` only if the application needs a new query.
5. Test: integration tests run all migrations against a fresh PostgreSQL 17 Testcontainer, so
   `scripts/test.sh backend` proves that the migration applies and that entities validate. Add a test that exercises
   the new data path.
6. Apply locally. Flyway runs at backend startup:
   ```bash
   scripts/deploy.sh               # Docker: rebuilds the backend image and migrates on start
   scripts/run-dev.sh restart      # dev mode: rebuilds the jar and migrates on start
   ```
7. Inspect (container engine via the compose command the scripts use, e.g. `docker compose` or `docker-compose`):
   ```bash
   docker-compose exec postgres psql -U aichat -d aichat -c '\d+ <table>'
   docker-compose exec postgres psql -U aichat -d aichat -c 'select version, description, success from flyway_schema_history order by installed_rank'
   ```

## Data model reference

`users` 1─n `conversations` 1─n `messages`; `conversations` n─1 `system_prompts`. `llm_executions` has one row per
LLM call (chat, compare, title, summary), with optional references to message, conversation and user
(`ON DELETE SET NULL`, so usage statistics survive deletions). `provider_settings` holds the admin overrides per
provider id. See the ER diagram in [docs/architecture.md](../../../docs/architecture.md#data-model).

## Recovering a local database

- Startup fails with a checksum mismatch after editing an applied migration: revert the edit and add a new migration.
  For throwaway local data only, `scripts/deploy.sh up --fresh` recreates the database (deletes all data).
- Startup fails with a schema validation error: the entity and the SQL disagree. Fix the entity or add a migration.
